answer: Each submission hangs on the shale of a task receipt, and the grove is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Written in a tight, ends on the cost register, it stays short. The violet of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. The design leans on per-epoch sampling audit, diluted when peers disagree, rewards vest against future work.
